## Proof

Let $Y_i = -\ln(1 - X_i)$. Since $X_i \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1)$, we have $1 - X_i \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1)$ as well. For $y \geq 0$:

$$P(Y_i \geq y) = P(-\ln(1-X_i) \geq y) = P(1 - X_i \leq e^{-y}) = P(X_i \geq 1 - e^{-y}) = e^{-y}.$$

Thus each $Y_i \sim \text{Exp}(1)$, the exponential distribution with rate $1$, having mean $E[Y_i] = 1$ and variance $\text{Var}(Y_i) = 1$.

Define $S_n = Y_1 + Y_2 + \cdots + Y_n$. Then $E[S_n] = n$ and $\text{Var}(S_n) = n$. We seek

$$\lim_{n \to \infty} P(S_n \geq n) = \lim_{n \to \infty} P(S_n \geq E[S_n]).$$

By the **Central Limit Theorem**, since the $Y_i$ are i.i.d. with finite mean $\mu = 1$ and finite variance $\sigma^2 = 1$,

$$\frac{S_n - n}{\sqrt{n}} \xrightarrow{d} Z \sim N(0,1).$$

Therefore,

$$P(S_n \geq n) = P\!\left(\frac{S_n - n}{\sqrt{n}} \geq 0\right) \xrightarrow{n \to \infty} P(Z \geq 0) = \frac{1}{2}.$$

**Verification via the Poisson–Gamma relationship.** Since $S_n \sim \text{Gamma}(n, 1)$, its survival function at $n$ is

$$P(S_n \geq n) = e^{-n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{n^k}{k!} = P(N_n \leq n-1),$$

where $N_n \sim \text{Poisson}(n)$. Applying the CLT to $N_n$ (with mean $n$, variance $n$):

$$P(N_n \leq n-1) = P\!\left(\frac{N_n - n}{\sqrt{n}} \leq \frac{-1}{\sqrt{n}}\right) \xrightarrow{n\to\infty} P(Z \leq 0) = \frac{1}{2},$$

confirming the result through an independent route.

### Conclusion

$$\boxed{\lim_{n\to\infty} P\!\left(-\ln(1-X_1) - \ln(1-X_2) - \cdots - \ln(1-X_n) \geq n\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
